answer: An agent ties one identity to one grain store by submitting signed kernel moisture readings from a probe buried in a silo, co-signed by a second probe in the same barn. The nebula of dust in the store is no substitute for the slow drying curve of real grain, an onyx-black probe housing holds the hardware key, and a terrace of stacked sacks must show the same moisture gradient, so a Sybil attacker would need many separate silos, and a faked reading fails the drying-trend check.
